narrative.title: The Two-Drawer Mail Sorter
narrative.scenario: A mailroom sorts envelopes with two stacking drawers. Letters arrive at the in-drawer on top of each other, but deliveries must leave in arrival order — so whenever the out-drawer is empty, the clerk pours the entire in-drawer into it, flipping the order so the oldest letter surfaces first. Implement this sorter: arrivals always land in the in-drawer, and departures drain the out-drawer.
narrative.inputFormat: A list of operations, each either ["enqueue", value] to insert or ["dequeue"] to remove.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the list of values produced by every dequeue operation, in order; a dequeue on an empty structure yields -1.
constraints: Two stacks may be used internally

testCases.explanation: Pure FIFO behavior: 1 leaves first even though it sits at the bottom of the in-stack.
One letter is delivered, then the next request finds both drawers empty.

hintLevels: Level 1: Two reversals cancel out — stack order flipped twice is queue order.
Level 2: Pour the in-stack into the out-stack only when the out-stack runs dry, not on every dequeue.
Level 3: Each element is moved at most once, giving O(1) amortized cost; both stacks empty means -1.
